events.title: Top Republican hangs massive scandal around Howard Lutnick’s neck: report
events.description: A top Senate Republican turned up the heat on Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick on Friday, accusing him of ignoring repeated warnings about suspected AI chip smuggling to China, while declining to back the embattled Trump official. "If Howard Lutnick wanted my support, perhaps he should have responded to my many letters,” Sen. Tom Cotton (R-AR), who chairs the Senate Intelligence Committee, said in an exclusive interview with The Wall Street Journal. President Donald Trump has continued to stand by Lutnick as lawmakers zero in on the Commerce Department’s handling of chip exports. While Cotton “stopped short” of calling for Lutnick’s ouster from the administration, he declined to offer him his support, the Journal reported. According to the Journal, Cotton added that if the president “has lost confidence in Lutnick, he should ask him to resign and move quickly so the Republican-led Senate can confirm a successor before Democrats take control in January.” Cotton said he urged Lutnick in October 2025 to investigate Megaspeed, a company suspected of diverting Nvidia chips to China. “And, more importantly, taking the threats of communist China more seriously,” he said in the interview. Commerce had been investigating the company since 2024 but declined to put it on a trade blacklist. Cotton said some administration officials were coming around to his position, but added, “I think we need to catalog the damage that’s been done.”
